the Jews in The Acts of the Apostles

author unknown · the work’s page · read it where the Jews first appears

Abstract written by a model

The Jews are a group made up of twelve tribes who hold a hope in the promise God made to their fathers. The records chiefly show their hostility toward Paul. It begins in the temple, where Jews from Asia seize him, stir up the crowd, and accuse him of teaching against the people, the law, and the place, and of bringing Greeks inside, wrongly assuming Trophimus was with him. Then more than forty bind themselves under a curse to neither eat nor drink until Paul is killed, but their plan is discovered. Next the high priest and principal men press Festus to send Paul to Jerusalem, plotting to kill him on the way, and bring grievous charges they cannot prove. The whole multitude cries that he should not live. Finally Paul says they accuse him over the hope of the promise and tried to kill him in the temple.

Narrative, section by section written by a model

4 sections; each heading opens the text

Chapter 21

The Jews from Asia see Paul in the temple, stir up the multitude, and lay hands on him. They cry out that he teaches everywhere against the people, the law, and the place, and that he brought Greeks into the temple, wrongly assuming he had brought Trophimus the Ephesian, whom they had seen with him in the city.

Chapter 23

More than forty Jews band together and bind themselves under a curse to neither eat nor drink until they have killed Paul. They tell the chief priests and elders to have the commanding officer bring Paul down, planning to kill him before he arrives, but their plan is discovered and Paul is moved out of their reach.

Chapter 25

The high priest and principal men of the Jews inform Festus against Paul and ask him to summon Paul to Jerusalem, plotting to kill him on the way. They come down to Caesarea and bring many grievous charges they cannot prove. Festus later says the whole multitude of the Jews petitioned him, crying that Paul ought not to live any longer.

Chapter 26

The Jews accuse Paul over the hope of the promise made to their fathers, and Paul says they know his way of life from his youth. He says they seized him in the temple and tried to kill him, and that he was sent to deliver them and the Gentiles from darkness to light.

Israel in Paul’s Letter to the Romans

author unknown · the work’s page · read it where Israel first appears

Abstract written by a model

Israel is a people privileged with adoption, glory, covenants, the giving of the law, service, promises and the fathers, and the line from which Christ came according to the flesh. Yet not all of Israel are truly Israel; only a remnant is saved. Pursuing a law of righteousness by works rather than faith, Israel stumbled over the stumbling stone. It has zeal for God without knowledge, is ignorant of God's righteousness, and seeks to establish its own, remaining a disobedient and contrary people to whom God stretched out his hands. The speaker prays for its salvation. Its chosen obtained what it sought while the rest were hardened. Its fall brought salvation and riches to the Gentiles, and a partial hardening lasts until the fullness of the Gentiles comes in. Finally, all Israel will be saved: enemies for the Gentiles' sake regarding the Good News, but beloved for the fathers' sake regarding election.

Chapter 9

The Israelites are described as possessing the adoption, glory, covenants, giving of the law, service, promises and the fathers, and as the people from whom Christ came according to the flesh. Not all who are of Israel are Israel; only a remnant will be saved, and Israel, pursuing a law of righteousness, did not reach it because it sought it by works and stumbled over the stumbling stone.

Chapter 10

Israel is the object of the speaker's heart's desire and prayer for salvation. They have zeal for God but not according to knowledge, were ignorant of God's righteousness, sought to establish their own, and did not subject themselves to God's righteousness. Though they heard and were warned of provocation by a non-nation, God says he stretched out his hands all day to them as a disobedient and contrary people.

Chapter 11

Israel did not obtain what it sought, while the chosen obtained it and the rest were hardened. Its fall brought salvation to the Gentiles and riches to the world, and a partial hardening has come on it until the fullness of the Gentiles comes in. The text says all Israel will be saved, and that they are enemies for the Gentiles' sake regarding the Good News but beloved for the fathers' sake regarding election.

Abstract written by a model

The Jews are a group described through acts of disbelief, wrongdoing, and opposition to Allah’s way. Some change words from their context, distort religion with their tongues, speak words of disobedience, and slander religion. They break their covenant, disbelieve in Allah’s revelations, slay prophets wrongfully, speak against Mary with tremendous calumny, hinder Allah’s way, and are cursed by Allah for disbelief, though a few believe. Some given a portion of Scripture believe idols and false deities and regard idolaters as more rightly guided than believers. Their wrongdoing leads Allah to forbid them good things previously lawful. The account also highlights their taking usury despite prohibition and devouring people’s wealth by false pretences. It unfolds from their distortions and disbelief through covenant-breaking and grave accusations to divine cursing and the forbidding of lawful good things.
